status: normal-quantile seed/domain repairs verified by focused tests and independent enclosures; remaining items are open
verified_repairs: NormalQuantile checks the open probability domain before using a seed or publishing any numeric approximation; exact median witnesses return zero.

Seed values and seed precision never act as numeric certificates. Only bounded hints (at most 128 bits, precision -64 through 0) are considered, and they are clamped to a certified bracket; other hints are ignored.

An adaptive finite CDF bracket replaces the fixed result-magnitude estimate and the seed-dependent recursive base case. Safeguarded Newton proposals alternate with midpoint steps if no result has been certified.

Every returned fine/unit-scale sample follows from explicit one-unit CDF/probability enclosures or an already certified integer bracket of width at most two. Positive precisions coarsen a certified unit-scale result.
All observed cancellation propagates through probability validation, bracket construction, CDF/density evaluation and root cache publication.

Independent directed MPFR sqrt/division/erfc bounds validate 560 adversarial-seed enclosures, while 112 extreme-coarse cases use independently certified finite bounds. Two additional MPFR cases cover probability 10^-300 with quantile magnitude above 32.
proof_outline: If A approximates Phi(x) and P approximates the probability at the same precision, A+2<=P proves Phi(x)<=p and A-2>=P proves Phi(x)>=p. Both samples have at most one unit of error.
Strict monotonicity of Phi turns the two endpoint inequalities into a quantile enclosure. Integer bracket endpoints at most two grid units apart fit within one unit of their rounded midpoint.
The seed and Newton density quotient only choose candidates. An unsuccessful proposal cannot change the bracket without a separately certified CDF sign comparison.
At least every second unsuccessful step uses an interior integer midpoint; certified sign comparisons contract the bracket. Ambiguous comparisons refine precision and never guess a direction.
On |x|<=R+1, pi<4 and e<4 imply phi(x)>2^(-(R+1)^2-2). The chosen working guard makes sufficiently accurate candidate endpoint probes separable, subject to the approximation precision ceiling.
Coarsening a unit-scale enclosure to precision p>=1 adds at most 2^-p approximation error and one-half unit of rounding error, totaling at most one output unit.
